title: Introduction to the Arts of Canada
description: An interdisciplinary examination of Canada's cultural identity and of current issues facing the arts in both French and English speaking Canada. Topics to be considered include aboriginal arts, theatre, history in art, visual and literary arts, music, multiculturalism, broadcasting and cultural policies.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ACAN 225, FA 225.

crossListedCourses.title: Introduction to the Arts of Canada

title: International Community Development Through Capacity Building
description: Students examine the role they can play to improve their communities in Canada and abroad. Topics include international community development issues and how economic disparities are threatening communities across the globe, including threats to the ecology, health, education, governance, peace and personal rights and freedoms. Examines how individuals, non-profit organizations, governments and social movements can build capacity for change in Canada and in other countries.

title: Social-Ecological Justice and Action for Planetary Health
description: Foundational understandings of Planetary Health and the climate crisis, drawing on Indigenous and western knowledge systems. Examines current governance structures that help and hinder our abilities to achieve local-to-global social-ecological justice. Topics include historiography of planetary health, socio-political power dynamics, relationality to the land, colonial violence, Indigenous resistance and resurgence, as well as pathways, policy solutions and change-making action for Planetary Health.

title: Public Sector Economics
description: An introduction to public sector economic principles and theories. Topics include market failures such as: public goods and externalities; taxation and public spending; effectiveness, efficiency, equity and political feasibility criteria for policy evaluation and review processes. Applied public sector economics and Indigenous economics are discussed.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 310, ADMN 403, ECON 100, ECON 103, ECON 103C, ECON 104, ECON 180, ECON 201, ENGR 280 (if taken prior to May 2012).

title: Introduction to Public Administration
description: An exploration of the external factors affecting contemporary public sector management in Canada, the changing structural and value context within which public servants work, the key processes in which they are engaged and how those processes are changing. Focus is primarily on the federal and provincial governments. Discusses municipal administration and Indigenous governance.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 311, HSD 404, POLI 350.

title: Leading and Managing in Public and Non-Profit Sectors
description: An examination of the skills of an effective manager in public and non-profit sector organizations and the interplay between management and key organizational processes such as planning, organizing, implementing and evaluating policies, programs and services. Management topics include managerial work, interpersonal and leadership skills, power and influence, conflict resolution, formal and informal communications, motivation and teamwork. A project on managing organizational change is used as a way to connect manager behaviours and organizational processes.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 312, ADMN 406.

title: Public Sector Research and Analysis
description: An introduction to qualitative and quantitative research methods in public and non-profit sector settings. Critical research methodologies are used to develop students’ own research project proposals. Topics include: research design; sampling and data analysis, ethnography, content analysis, interviews, mixed methods research, research ethics, Indigenous Knowledge and data governance and public engagement methods.

title: Public Sector Communications
description: Contemporary communications theory and application with focus on the communication tools in the public and non-profit sectors. Topics include: developing technically and strategically sound written, verbal and interpersonal communication skills for internal and external audiences; basic media relations; creating online/electronic content; synthesizing information for briefing notes, proposals and news releases; and how to engage elected officials and executive, community and stakeholders using effective and inclusive communication processes.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 316, ENGL 302, ENSH 304.

title: Indigenous Governance in Canada
description: Provides foundational knowledge on concepts, themes and topics needed to understand and appreciate Indigenous governance. Covers historical and contemporary challenges facing Indigenous peoples, including the Indian Act and its impact on Indigenous governance. Topics are organized by eras beginning with pre-contact Indigenous governance systems and European colonization of Indigenous governance, then proceeding to Indigenous resistance and revival of the inherent right, nation building and ways Indigenous Nations are implementing self-government along with its challenges and successes.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 330, ADMN 470 (if taken in same topic), ADMN 548 (if taken in same topic), ICDG 301.

title: Governance for Planetary Health
description: Provides students a foundational understanding of Planetary Health from an interdisciplinary lens. Focuses on transformative governance strategies embracing the environmental, political, economic, social and cultural dimensions to achieve high standards of health, well-being, equity and ecological prosperity. Explores pathways and policy solutions at the local, regional, national and global levels for reconciling natural and human systems.

title: Managing Service Delivery
description: Explores challenges facing public sector managers who develop or transform public services with a strong focus on service recipients. Examines the drivers of service transformation, surveys the ways that public services can be reformed; and presents frameworks to assess service needs, engage service recipients and stakeholders, implement new delivery arrangements (including networks and partnerships), manage across boundaries, conduct performance measurement and ensure accountability.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete 1 of:
    • ADMN311 - Introduction to Public Administration (1.5)
    • POLI350 - Introduction to Public Administration (1.5)

title: Non-profit Governance and Management
description: An overview of management in Canada’s non‐profit and voluntary sector. Examines the size, scope, structure, functions, value bases and uniqueness of the non‐profit sector, plus the differences among the non‐profit, public and private sectors. Topics include board governance, leadership and board relations, stakeholder relations, strategic planning, volunteer recruitment and motivation, and client engagement. Students analyze how management concepts, models, principles and techniques have validity as applied in the context of non‐profit and voluntary sector organizations.

title: Public Sector Project Management
description: Provides an understanding of project management; differences between private, non-profit and public sector project management; and how the dynamics of change and leadership impact project success. Topics include: what project management is and is not; project leadership; risk management; project planning; scheduling and critical path; problem solving; project governance, accountability and transparency; project sponsor role; change management including assessing readiness for change; setting up change governance structures to sustain change; best practices; and project evaluation.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 411, ADMN 470 (if taken in the same topic).

title: The Public Policy Process
description: An introduction to the policy process in the public sector. Includes analysis of current theories of policy-making and examines case studies from Canadian contexts. Topics include: policy formation; the policy communication process; the structural aspects of policy execution; and the human dimensions of implementation and coordination of policies in public sector organizations.
recommendations: • ADMN 310 and/or ADMN 314 recommended prior to ADMN 420.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 420, ADMN 465.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete 1 of:
    • ADMN311 - Introduction to Public Administration (1.5)
    • POLI350 - Introduction to Public Administration (1.5)

title: Financial Management
description: Provides a foundation in public sector financial management, focused on the needs of government managers. Topics include: government financial statements and their analysis; public sector accounting standards and financial reporting; operational and capital budgeting; public sector financial management; cost management and control; accountability and performance measurement. Covers all levels of government in Canada: municipal; provincial and federal. Familiarity with the use of Microsoft Excel required.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 421, ADMN 448.

title: Ethical Public Management
description: An exploration of value and ethical dilemmas which confront public and quasi-public sector officials in the workplace. Focuses on process dilemmas related to political neutrality, confidentiality, privacy, fairness and accountability, as well as issues related to good, just and legitimate public policy. Students have an opportunity to develop their own moral reasoning skills and apply them in case studies.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 422, ADMN 554.

title: Local Government and Governance
description: Discusses local government legislative frameworks, functions, financing, leadership, policy development and public administration. Explores the nature of local governance and relationships between and within regions, special purpose bodies and Indigenous governments. Focuses on local government in British Columbia, but includes comparative examples.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 423, ADMN 545.

title: Public Sector Human Resource Management
description: Examines various aspects of the human resource function within public sector organizations and compares current theory and practice in: human resource planning; job analysis and design; recruitment and selection; performance management; training; career planning; staff development; and occupational health and safety.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 431A, ADMN 431, ADMN 447, ADMN 531.

title: Labour Relations Negotiations
description: Examines successful negotiation skills, conflict management styles, goals and principles of positional and interest-based negotiation, the labour relations climate and bargaining in response to human resource issues such as equity and diversity, compensation, workplace safety and health and employee pensions. Topics include: negotiating compensation issues, discipline and grievance and developing a collective agreement. Coursework involves group participation in negotiating a workplace issue and participation in a labour-management simulation.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 431B, ADMN 431.

title: Foundations for Program Evaluation
description: Provides an overview of the concepts, models and issues in evaluation. Students will be introduced to the practice of program evaluation; determining which evaluation questions and approaches to use, developing an evaluation plan, planning collection of data, establishing reporting processes and considering ethical issues in evaluation. Students will be introduced to contemporary issues in the field such as environmental, social, political and cultural dynamics of an evaluation context.
recommendations: • An advanced understanding of statistical methods is not required for this course, but knowledge of and ability to apply basic concepts in statistics and research methods is expected.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 437, ADMN 537.

title: Urban and Regional Development
description: Examines economic forces influencing settlement patterns, growth and other characteristics of towns, cities and regions. Provides a theoretical and historical basis for analyzing and predicting how urban areas evolve and how public policies may affect patterns of growth and change. Topics include: regional economics; economic development; growth policy; urban land use patterns; how land and housing markets function; how land use regulation affects these markets; urban environmental problems; urban transportation; and emerging spatial patterns.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 445, ECON 312.

title: Local Government Land Use Planning
description: Provides an overview of land use planning principles and regulations to local government administrators and staff, focusing on small and mid-sized communities. Topics include: history; regulatory framework in BC; rural and small town planning, growth management and regional planning; neighbourhood, local area and community planning; zoning; mainstreet, strip and commercial planning; residential planning; permits and other regulatory mechanisms; public information and participation; and environmental and heritage planning.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 446, ADMN 470 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Local Government Law
description: Analysis of legislation and court decisions applicable to local governments in British Columbia, including the Community Charter. Designed to familiarize non-lawyers with local government law and legal issues which arise in relation to local government activities and how to read case law and legislation.

title: Intergovernmental Relations in Canada
description: Examines relations between federal, provincial/territorial, municipal and Indigenous governments in Canada across a range of complex policy areas. Topics include managing intergovernmental disputes, the role of fiscal transfers and the changing nature of our federation. Individual and/or team projects explore the state of our social, economic and environmental union.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 462, ADMN 470 (if taken in the same topic), ADMN 547, POLI 462, POLI 490 (if taken in the same topic).
  • A combined undergraduate and graduate course.

title: Contemporary Topics in Administration
description: A study of selected topics drawn from the current literature and practices in public administration or related fields.
supplementalNotes: • May be offered as a joint undergraduate and graduate class.
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics.

title: Strategic Planning and Implementation
description: Examines strategic planning processes and how strategic goals can be implemented in public sector organizations. Strategic planning topics include stakeholder analysis; developing mission, value and vision statements; environmental scanning; transforming strategic plans into policies and programs; management tactics; and assessing organizational performance. Implementation topics include: deploying resources; quality control; strategic communication; budgeting; team building; problem solving; progress assessment; completion; and evaluation.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of ADMN 477, ADMN 412, ADMN 470 (if taken in the same topic), ADMN 577.

title: Directed Studies
description: Directed reading and/or a research project under the supervision of a Faculty Member.
preAndCorequisites: • Permission of the school.

title: Introduction to Art Education I
description: A foundation course for those interested in teaching art in school or community settings. Working in various studio activities, students build knowledge and skill in studio art while considering how those experiences may be adapted for young learners. Art education topics include artistic development, critical and cultural perspectives on art and teaching methodologies.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AE 103A, AE 103, AE 100, AE 101, AE 204, ED-A 701, EDCI 307, EDCI 307A, EDCI 307B, EDUC 307.
  • Students planning to emphasize art in their degree program should register in this course.

title: Introduction to Art Education II
description: A continuing investigation of studio processes and art concepts as well as methods of instruction appropriate to children and youths in classroom and community settings.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AE 103B, AE 103, AE 100, AE 101, AE 204, ED-A 701, EDCI 307, EDCI 307A, EDCI 307B, EDUC 307.
  • Students planning to emphasize art in their degree program should register in this course.

title: Image Development
description: A survey of methods and practices of innovative image transformation and development of skills and techniques through studio exploration. Instructional applications in various learning environments are considered.

title: Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques
description: Introduction to the wheel through basic cylinder forms and hand-building skills. Glazing and the process of studio practice are explored through project-based assignments. Historic and contemporary ceramic perspectives and connections to Art Education curriculum are investigated.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 303A, AE 303.

title: Intermediate Ceramics Studio Explorations
description: Advanced development of studio practice of wheel, glazing and hand forming techniques. Explores issues of design, content, form and surface. Investigation of historical and contemporary ceramic perspectives and connections to Art Education curriculum.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 303B, AE 303.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete 1 of:
    • AE303A - Introduction to Ceramics Wheel and Hand Techniques (1.5)
    • AE309 - Introduction to Ceramic Hand Building Techniques (1.5)

title: Drawing
description: Development of skills and teaching methods in drawing through studio exploration. Instructional applications in various learning environments are considered.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 305, AE 302.

title: Painting
description: Development of skills and teaching methods in painting through studio exploration. Instructional applications in various learning environments are considered.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AE 306, AE 302.
  • Supply list available from MacLaurin A430.

title: Printmaking
description: An introduction to printmaking including its history, related concepts and selected studio techniques. Exploration and experimentation are emphasized as a means of skill development. Instructional applications in various learning environments are considered.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 307, AE 300.

title: Sculpture
description: Development of skills and teaching methods in sculpture through studio exploration. Instructional applications in various learning environments are considered.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 308, AE 301.

title: Introduction to Ceramic Hand Building Techniques
description: Exploration of introductory sculptural and functional techniques through original project-based assignments including pinch, coil, slab, plus surface decoration and basic glazing. Investigation of historical and contemporary ceramic perspectives and connections to Art Education curriculum.

title: Introduction to Visual Design
description: Introduction to the theory and practice of visual design and its role in our lives. Studio work is project-based and may include package design, brand design, wayfinding and typography.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 310, AE 304.

title: Design Thinking
description: Inquiry guided by the design thinking process informs creative problem solving in the art and design context. Studio exploration involves applying the elements and principles of design to art, design and community challenges.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 200, AE 311.

title: Community Art Education for Social Change
description: An introduction to community art education in venues such as community organizations, public spaces, museums, and galleries. Exploration of studio practices unique to community art education and the development of an art exhibition and related educational activities as a contributor to community engagement and social change.

title: Responding to Art
description: Methods of teaching art through appreciation, creative response and critique with an emphasis on Canadian art. An investigation of art from the perspectives of aesthetics, art history and art criticism. Students prepare educational materials.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 316, AE 317.

title: Photography
description: Basic approaches to photography as an art medium. An exploration of concepts and methods appropriate to elementary and secondary classrooms and other educational settings from simple technologies such as photograms and pinhole photography to 35 mm cameras and darkroom procedures.

title: Digital Arts
description: An introduction to contemporary digital arts which may include graphics, animation, modelling, audio, video, or website construction using a critically reflective lens that considers technical and aesthetic concepts.

title: Visual Design for Marketing, Advocacy and Persuasion
description: Focus is primarily on design for marketing within the context of its persuasive role in education and educational advocacy. Explores visual design as a problem-solving approach in the development of high impact communication through a combination of theory and studio practice.

title: Special Studies
description: Studies of selected topics in the theory and practice of art education.
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics with permission of the department to a maximum of 6 units.

title: Studio Based Artistic Inquiry
description: Introduces students to artistic inquiry using art methods and materials to examine questions and develop ideas through studio-based assignments. Open to students at all artistic levels working in medium(s) of their choice.

title: Advanced Digital Arts
description: An advanced exploration of contemporary digital arts using graphics, animation, modelling, audio, video, or website construction. Students have the opportunity to explore individual media projects related to areas of interest. Emphasizes advanced digital media theory and practice.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AE 422, AE 402J.
preAndCorequisites:
• Complete all of:
    • AE322 - Digital Arts (1.5)

title: Healthy Ageing

groupFilter1.name: School of Public Health and Social Policy

description: Adopting a life-course perspective, this course will explore the determinants of good health in old age. Those determinants range from biology to the urban environment, from early childhood experience to the availability of supportive services in the community, from education and health literacy to clinical prevention and self-care. Policies and programs from Canada and around the world that support healthy ageing are examined.

title: Chronic Disease and Ageing

groupFilter1.name: School of Public Health and Social Policy

description: Chronic diseases are very prevalent among the elderly, and their management has a major influence on the health, functionality and quality of life of older people. The growing body of evidence and experience in the delivery of high quality, safe, effective care is examined and the design of systems that encourage and support high quality care are explored. The role of chronic disease self-management and social support networks is an important focus.

title: First-Year Seminar on Art, Images, Experience

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Experiential introduction to the diverse contexts in which we encounter art and images today. Participants may engage in a variety of hands-on activities with art objects, meet with guests who use art and images in various professional contexts, and explore, in a small-group format, current issues pertaining to the study of art.
supplementalNotes: • Normally class size is limited.

title: Exploring World Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of visual culture and artistic expressions from prehistory to the present. Students learn the fundamentals of visual analysis to understand and appreciate the world's art. Comprehension of the similarities that connect visual traditions around the globe, as well as understanding of cultural differences.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 120, HA 120.

title: Understanding Visual Communication

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of the impact of visual imagery on the lives of individuals and communities. Introduces the idea that images constitute a complex system of visual communication, giving essentials of visual analysis and interpretation. Content may include, advertising, branding and the internet, comics, video game imagery and traditional artistic forms.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 121, HA 121.

title: Artists' Materials and Techniques

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of the techniques used by artists throughout history, in western and nonwestern cultures. The development of art technology is considered in its historical and social contexts. Period or area of emphasis may vary.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 200, HA 200, HA 310.

title: Confronting the Object

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Provides first-hand experience working with objects in collections. Emphasizes the recovery of the historical context and the ways in which artifacts are presented in museums and other cultural institutions.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 202, HA 202.

title: The Classical Tradition in Western Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to the influence of Greco-Roman artistic traditions on subsequent periods of European civilization. The classical inheritance in terms of both style and iconography is examined in a variety of selected monuments from the Middle Ages through to the 20th century.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 222, HA 222.

title: Introduction to Western Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to the aims and methods of architectural history using case-studies of monuments from the history of Western architecture from archaic Greece to the present. Issues considered can include: changing patterns of patronage; shifts in building-types, features, and structural systems; and influential theories of design.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 223, HA 223.

title: Monuments of South and Southeast Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to Indigenous, Hindu, Buddhist and Islamic world views through the study of religious monuments and ideas in South and Southeast Asia, including philosophical and religious principles underlying architecture, painting, sculpture and textiles. Emphasizes the learning of analytical and writing skills essential to these areas of Asian art history.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 230, HA 230.

title: Sacred Form in South and Southeast Asian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to select forms and symbols in Buddhist and Hindu art. Focus may include figurative, geometric, informal and formal arts, in lasting and ephemeral materials. Provides students with the basic skills to describe and analyze arts of the region created in religious or spiritual contexts.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 232, HA 232.

title: Encountering Renaissance Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of key works of art and architecture by major creative minds in Europe during the Renaissance (1400-1550), such as Donatello, Alberti, Leonardo, Michelangelo, Bosch and Sophonisba Anguissola.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 234, HA 234.

title: The Image of the Artist

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Investigates how artists and cultures create artistic identities. Topics may include the social and economic status of artists, theories of creativity and genius, the art market, guilds and academies, self-portraits, artists' houses and tombs, cross-cultural understandings of creators and the role of social media, video and the internet in the creation of artistic identity.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 241, HA 241.

title: Introduction to the Arts of Islam

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the art and architecture of Islam around the world, beginning with the rise of Islam and continuing to the present.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 251, HA 251, HIST 251.

title: Modern and Contemporary Art Icons

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An in-depth introduction to the life and career of modern or contemporary art icons such as Joseph Beuys, Barbara Hepworth, Andy Warhol, Georgia O'Keeffe, Pablo Picasso, Varvara Stepanova or Marina Abramovic. Studied artists vary.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 260, HA 260.
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics to a maximum of 3 units.

title: Art History and the Lens

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the role of images in various social and cultural venues. Case studies may examine the relationships between photographic images and exhibitions, publications, film, artwork, and other media within the context of different cultures and social practices.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 264, HA 264.

title: Introduction to Canadian Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of principal periods, media, practitioners, and movements in the history of non-native Canadian art and architecture from first settlement to today. The arts of English and French Canada are considered, and the political, social and cultural settings in which they have been made is explored.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 268, HA 268.
  • Several classes may be taught at the Art Gallery of Greater Victoria.

title: Indigenous Arts, Local Themes and Global Challenges

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores values and philosophies conveyed by First Nations arts of the Northwest Coast. Examines how older and contemporary arts reflect human connections with the environment, roles of arts and artists in 21st-century events and activism, arts and the Internet, diversity of cultural expressions and relevance to global challenges such as climate change.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 284, HA 284, HA 382A (if taken prior to Sep-Dec 1999).

title: Selected Themes in Art History and Visual Studies

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to a selected theme or area of art-historical study that is not covered in other AHVS courses at this level. Content may vary from year to year.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 292, HA 292 (if taken in the same topic).
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics with permission of the department.

title: Introduction to Film Analysis

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An investigation of film culture and its relationship to social and historical contexts. Focuses on active readings of cinematic texts, searching for the possible meanings of individual shots, sequences and narrative structures. Involves a three hour lecture or screening and a one hour tutorial a week.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 295A, HA 295, HA 295A.

title: Introduction to Film Studies

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An investigation of film culture and its relationship to social and historical contexts. Considers key issues in film scholarship, critical strategies and theoretical concepts. Involves a three hour lecture or screening and a one hour tutorial a week.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 295B, HA 295, HA 295B.

title: Masterpieces of Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An analysis of selected works of art central to the traditions of world art.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 300A, HA 300A.

title: Fakes, Forgeries and Fraud

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Case studies examine art crimes in different regions and periods. Introduces historical, legal and forensic issues related to authentication and object recovery.

title: The Destruction of Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines the intentional damaging of art and architecture in times of conflict. Central themes include iconoclasm, political and religious censorship, looting and vandalism. Case studies cover different regions and periods while focusing on the motivations of groups and individuals.

title: Making Art History

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Experiential research into objects and applied arts. Students engage with objects to develop technical and social insight into their histories and cultural values. Topics vary.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310A, HA 310A (if taken in the same topic).
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics with permission of the department to a maximum of 3 units.

title: Presenting Digital Art History

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores the key shifts and art historical implications of the digital revolution. Students also investigate the graphic components of their identities as emerging scholars and digital citizens, developing skills in industry-standard software and applications for effective and compelling presentations.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310B, HA 310B.

title: Digital Tools for Art History and Visual Studies

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: In this lab-based course students use digital tools in relation to art history and visual studies. They explore a variety of new technologies to approach, shape and develop research projects. Topics include: image mark-up and augmentation, digital curation, information visualization and mapping, contemporary and historical environment creation.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310C, HA 310C.
  • No programming or coding experience is required.

title: Environmental Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of examples of Environmental Art to the present day, beginning with the 1960s Land Art movement. Topics may include: earthworks, environmental art, performances and actions by artists ranging from Robert Smithson, Walter de Maria, Ana Mendieta, Andy Goldsworthy, Alice Aycock.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310D, HA 310D.

title: Topics in Craft and Communities

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the major craft movements in British Columbia from the late nineteenth century to the present focusing on the changing views of craft within various contexts such as the Arts and Crafts Movement, the Canadian Craft Guild, the Canada Council for the Arts, indigenous rights and contemporary DIY political action.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310E, HA 310E (if taken in the same topic).
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics with permission of the department to a maximum of 3 units.

title: Modern and Contemporary Design

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Focuses on the cultural roles of design in finding creative solutions to basic human needs, such as shelter, clothing, useful objects, visual communications, transportation and built environments in a variety of social contexts.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 310F, HA 310F.

title: Fashion Curation and Art History

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of fashion as art. Includes an experiential component around the display of garments in local museums and galleries. May include curatorial requirements specific to clothing, the history and significance of associated technologies, an introduction to the ethics of specific designs and designers around the globe.

title: Visual Intelligence

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Introduces new research in the field of visual intelligence. Explores Leonardo da Vinci and other artists' methods of open-ended inquiry and effective problem solving, through observation, visual analysis and application. Students engage in self-generated research questions, applying historical and contemporary tools from global artmaking to their learning.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 311A, HA 311A.

title: Looking and the History of Perception

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A thematic introduction to issues of visuality, brain and perceptual functioning in past and present societies around the world. Content may include, the perception of space, motion and colour; pictures, symbols and signs; images and abstract thinking; art and the imitation of nature; tradition and its impact on seeing; new insights from the field of neuroarthistory.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 311B, HA 311B.

title: The Sacred Gaze

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An exploration of ways of seeing that invest images, buildings, people and places with spiritual significance. Investigates key aspects of vision and imagery in a variety of religious traditions.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 311C, HA 311C.

title: Artists and Art History in Popular Culture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines the portrayal of art movements, artists, art works, art historians, and art critics in popular media such as radio, film, television or comics.

title: History of Video Games and Interactive Media

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores the cultural role of video games as an interactive visual medium. Classes focus on influential games and designers, new genres and technological innovations, the integration of visual art, sound, narrative and interactive game play, questions of representation, race, gender, games as art, representations of art and artists and other themes.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 311E, TS 320 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Horror Video Games

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An inquiry into the nature of fear and the grotesque in digital games as an interactive visual medium. Examines a variety of mainstream and independent digital games for their use of horror tropes. Employs various theoretical perspectives to investigate relevant digital games.

title: Gender, Identity and Film

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines representations of women and by women, in a variety of film forms (experimental, documentary, narrative) and within a range of historical periods. Emphasis is placed on feminist theories of representation, visual pleasure, spectatorship and subjectivity and on analyses of key films.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 312, HA 312.

title: Special Topics in The Art of the Garden

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Focuses on key gardens throughout the world from the earliest times to present. Special attention is paid to intersections between nature, religion, power, plant symbolism, art and architecture. Also examines the garden’s various social functions.
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics to a maximum of 3 units.

title: The Art of Power in South Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines works of visual culture from South Asia from prehistory to the present that express power.

title: Late Antique and Early Christian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the art and architecture of the Mediterranean world from the origins of Christian art in the third century CE to the onset of Iconoclasm in the eighth century. In addition to a detailed examination of surviving monuments and art objects, an emphasis is placed on the sources of Christian iconography and the relationship between art, theology and liturgy.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 321, HA 321.

title: Byzantine Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the art and architecture of the Byzantine empire and its culturally dependent areas from the period of Iconoclasm through to the fall of Constantinople in 1453 and beyond. The emphasis is on an examination of surviving monuments in Greece, Turkey, southern Italy, the Balkans and Russia.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 323, HA 323.

title: Ancient and Medieval Jewish Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the visual and material culture of Judaism in Israel and among the communities of the Diaspora from the first century CE to the 16th century CE. Major topics of interest are: the architectural evolution of the synagogue; changing attitudes to the role of figural art in a religious context; the arts of the book; and the artistic interactions with the visual traditions of Christian and Muslim communities.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 324, HA 324.

title: Early Medieval Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the arts and architecture of western Europe in the period c. 600-1150 CE. Topics to be considered include Anglo-Saxon, Carolingian, Ottonian, and Romanesque art.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 326, HA 326.

title: Gothic Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the art and architecture of western Europe from the reconstruction of St. Denis c. 1140 to the beginnings of Renaissance art in Florence c. 1400. Focuses primarily on architecture in northern Europe and on painting in Italy, with a concentration on artists from the cities of Florence, Rome and Siena.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 328, HA 328.

title: People and Possessions in Medieval Households

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores the furniture, fixtures, furnishings and tapestries in the medieval home. May include objects and the life course, spaces and everyday life, gender and the home.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 329, HA 329.

title: Early Arts of South Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Case studies in the arts in South Asia from the Indus Valley Civilization to the 11th century. The development of Hindu and Buddhist art, architecture and patronage is examined in relation to historical, philosophical and religious backgrounds. Selections from treatises on art and aesthetics are read in translation.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 330A, HA 330, HA 330A.
  • Normally to be offered in alternate years with AHVS 333A, AHVS 333B.

title: Later Arts of South Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the arts of South Asia, including the Himalayan region and Tibet, from the eighth century up to the 20th. Emphasis is on regional variations in Buddhist and Hindu art, the introduction of new ideas, art forms and styles with the establishment of Islamic rule and the role of colonialism and nationalism in the formation of the region's modern visual culture.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 330B, HA 330, HA 330B.

title: The Body in Indian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores the representation of the human body ranging from the erotic to the spiritual in Hindu and Buddhist art. Case studies include sculpture, painting, film, poetry and myth.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 330C, HA 330C, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Bollywood and Popular Visual Culture in India, 1950s onwards

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines popular Indian visual culture through the media of photography and film. Against a backdrop of Indian classical, folk, modern and contemporary, rural and urban art histories, select Bollywood films from the 1950s to the present are examined in class lectures, film screenings and readings. Styles featured range from historical, social realist and nationalist to stylized, idealist and moral narratives.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 332A, HA 332A, HA 337 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Bollywood Global and Popular Visual Culture, India and Diaspora, 1990s onwards

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of popular visual culture of India from classical, modern and contemporary art-historical and cultural perspectives. Themes of gender, identity, postcoloniality and national/global dynamics are addressed through screenings of select Bollywood films from the 1990s to today. Films made in India alternate with films which move into diasporic spaces in the UK, Canada and USA.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 332B, HA 332B, HA 337 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Early Arts of Southeast Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the arts of Southeast Asia, starting with prehistoric and contemporary tribal/indigenous cultures, up to the arrival of Islam. Discussion includes the majority of countries in the region, with emphasis on Indonesia. Monumental and personal arts relating to Hindu, Buddhist and Primal religious communities are discussed with attention to gender and historiography. Indigenous texts and film are used as source materials and basis for discussion.
supplementalNotes:
• Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 333A, HA 333, HA 333A.
  • Normally to be offered in alternate years with AHVS 330A, AHVS 330B.

title: Later Arts of Southeast Asia

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Case studies in the arts of Southeast Asia, from the arrival of Islam through the colonial and up through the modern period. Local definitions of art, the role of the artist in society and issues of patronage are discussed against a background of continuity and change. Indigenous texts and film are used as sources.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 333B, HA 333, HA 333B.

title: Special Topics in Contemporary Asian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of themes and issues in contemporary Asian art through case-studies in select national, regional and/or global contexts. Analyzes artists' careers, art institutions and art discourses, including the arrival of contemporary Asian art into western art historical consciousness.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 337, HA 337 (if taken in the same topic).
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics.

title: Modern and Contemporary Chinese Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Survey of modern and contemporary Chinese art. Topics may include: transition from earlier Chinese art to Chinese modernism; art during the Cultural Revolution; themes of nudity; landscape and gender; performance art; all in ongoing dialogue with traditional Chinese aesthetics and global movements.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 337A, AHVS 337 (if taken in the same topic), AHVS 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Modern and Contemporary Southeast Asian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Case studies in modern and contemporary Southeast Asian Art. Topics may include: transitions from earlier art practices to local, national and regional modernisms; independence movements and deepening globalization; identity, human rights, gender, ecology, and performance art; and dialogue with Indigenous and global aesthetics and movements.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 337B, AHVS 337 (if taken in the same topic), AHVS 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Special Topics in Premodern Asian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of themes and issues in premodern Asian art through case-studies in specific regional and/or temporal contexts.Topic: Popular Prints in China and Japan.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 338, HA 338 (if taken in the same topic).
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics.

title: The Global Renaissance

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Thematic investigation of artistic exchange between Europe, Asia, and the Americas during the 16th c. in the context of emerging globalism and nation states.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 339, HA 339, HA 341B.

title: Art in Renaissance Florence

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines the birth of Renaissance art and architecture in Florence. Works of art and artists' careers are examined within the context of themes such as: patronage; materials and methods; and religious and intellectual climate. It explores the city's unique sense of identity and destiny.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 341A, HA 341, HA 341A.

title: Michelangelo and Leonardo

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An investigation of the art and times of the two Renaissance artists. Topics include the creative process, the role of drawings, artist-patron relations, materials and methods of their art production and biographical constructions.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 341C, HA 341C.

title: Baroque Art in Italy 1550-1700

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Thematic investigation of painting, sculpture, and architecture in Italy during the Baroque, 1550-1700. Artists to be considered include Caravaggio, The Carracci, Bernini, Artemisia Gentileschi, Pietro da Cortona and Borromini.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 342A, HA 342, HA 342A.

title: Experiencing Baroque Painting

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Investigation of 17th c. painting in Italy, England, Holland, Flanders, and Spain in the context of international exchange and exploration. Artists may include Caravaggio, Artemisia Gentileschi, Rembrandt, Rubens, Vermeer, Judith Leyster, Anthony van Dyck, Ribera and Velasquez.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 342B, HA 342, HA 342B.

title: Gender and Sexuality in European Art 1400-1800

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of gender and sexuality as factors in making and interpreting art.

title: Collecting Cultures in Early Modern Europe

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines the practices of collecting in the context of European expansion and colonialism from 1500-1700.

title: Art in Venice 1500-1800

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Thematic investigation of art and architecture in Venice and the Veneto from 1500-1800. Content may include artistic identity, patronage, the art market, villa culture, and art for the domestic interior.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 343A, HA 343, HA 343A.

title: The 18th Century in Northern Europe

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A consideration of art and architecture in northern Europe, especially France and Britain, during the 18th century. Emphasis is placed on examining works of art within the contexts of political ideologies, social roles, and theoretical debate.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 343B, HA 343, HA 343B.

title: Special Topics in The Lives of Artists

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A critical examination of an artist's work. May include one or two artists.
recommendations: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics.
repeatableCatalogText: May be taken more than once for credit in different topics to a maximum of 3 units.

title: The Art of Travel 1200-1600

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Uses art, architecture and material culture to analyze medieval and early Modern travel experiences. Examines topics concerned with travel, such as spiritual quest, warfare, adventure and social display.

title: The Art of Travel 1600 to Present Day

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Uses art, architecture and material culture to analyze topics concerned with travel, such as trade, exploration, colonization and cultural tourism.

title: People and Things in the Early Modern Domestic Interior

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A critical investigation of the material culture of the home in Early Modern Europe (1400-1800) in the context of world trade and exploration. Examines the means by which household objects shape the dynamic social processes of cultural exchange and identity formation at the local, regional, and global level. Media to be considered may include jewelry, textiles, clothing, ceramics, furniture, prints, maps, portraits, paintings and sculptures.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 345, HA 345.

title: Visual Culture in Jane Austen's World

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines the visual culture of late Georgian and Regency England (c. 1760-1837), including painting, architecture, gardens, fashion, textile production, print culture, spectacle, professional and amateur arts. Considers the broader global context and assesses modern film and video interpretations of the period.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 346C, HA 346C.

title: Art and Architecture of the Safavid and Mughal Empires

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to key artworks (architecture, painting, textiles, weapons, jewelry) of the Persian Safavids and Indian Mughals, two contemporaneous early modern Islamic Empires.

title: Introduction to Islamic Archaeology

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to the archaeological investigation of the Islamic world. Covering a period from the seventh to the 19th century, the course employs case studies to examine urban life, religious identity, agriculture, trade and communications in the Middle East, North Africa, and the Iberian Peninsula.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 348, HA 348.

title: Islam and the West: Artistic Contacts, 1500-1900

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of the different modes of artistic contact between the Islamic world and the West from the 16th to the end of the 19th century. The developing artistic dialogue is examined in the context of the political and cultural history of this period. Traces the changing representations of the Islamic world in European painting and book illustration, the growth of Orientalist aesthetics in Europe and the introduction of Western themes into the arts of Turkey, Syria, Iran and India.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 349, HA 349.

title: Painting in Medieval Islam

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of painting in Islam from the 11th to the 15th century. Concentrates on the arts of the book.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 351A, HA 351A.

title: Painting in Iran

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of painting in Iran from the 15th to the 19th century. The course concentrates on the arts of the book.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 351B, HA 351B.

title: The Genesis of Islamic Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of the background, origins, and evolution of early Islamic art and architecture from the seventh century rise of Islam to the end of the ninth century. Investigates the fundamentals of Islam as a faith, Islam's relationship to the pre-Islamic past and the theoretical problem of creating a new visual culture to serve a new religion and society.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 352, HA 351, HA 352.

title: Medieval Islamic Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: The high medieval art and architecture of Islam from the 10th century to the Mongol invasions of the mid-13th century. Focuses on the medieval ideal of Islamic unity and the historic fragmentation of Islam into different, often opposed, regional and cultural entities. Major themes are the emergence of Turkish peoples as the dominant political rulers of the Near East and the impact of Latin and Byzantine Christendom on Islamic visual culture.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 354, HA 351, HA 354.

title: Old Kingdom Arts of Egypt

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of ancient Egyptian visual culture from its prehistoric roots to c. 1650 BCE, with a focus on the first great era of pyramid construction.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 355A, HA 355, HA 355A, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: New Kingdom Arts of Egypt

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of ancient Egyptian visual culture during the high empire period, c. 1550-1070 BCE. Subsequent eras may also be considered.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 355B, HA 355, HA 355B, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Arts of Mediterranean Islam, 13th- 20th Centuries

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: The art and architecture of Islam in the lands bordering the Mediterranean (Spain, Palestine, Syria and Turkey), from the mid-13th to the 20th century. Major areas of emphasis are the Nasrid dynasty of Spain, the Mamluk dynasty of Egypt and the Ottoman sultanate of Turkey.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 357, HA 353, HA 357.

title: Art of the Sultans and Emperors of India

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to art and architecture of the Islamic lands and peoples of South and Central Asia from the 12th to the 19th century. Content may include the arts of Mughal India, the Taj Mahal, the role of the British Raj in art and architecture.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 358, HA 353, HA 358.

title: Islamic Arts from the Mongol Conquests to Modernity

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examination of the art and architecture of major dynasties, such as the Ilkhanids, Timurids, and Safavids, from the impact of the Mongol conquests in 1221 to the 19th century.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 359, HA 359.

title: Modern Art in Europe and North America, 1900 to 1945

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Beginning with a brief examination of the European avant-garde in the late 19th century, the course analyzes in depth such 20th century movements as Cubism, Expressionism, Futurism, Constructivism, Social Realism and Surrealism. The European impact on modernist practices in America is also investigated.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 362A, HA 362A.

title: Art in Europe and North America, 1945 to present

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of directions taken in postwar art. Emphasis on the demise of the Modernist movement and the emergence of Postmodernism. Singled out for investigation are such areas as Abstract Expressionism, Minimalism, Pop Art, conceptual and performance art, environmental art and photo-based practices.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 362B, HA 362B.

title: Critical Issues in Contemporary Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines selected examples of contemporary art in the context of critical debates, art institutions, the art market and activism. Geographic areas of focus may vary.

title: The Cinema and Modern Art Movements

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An examination of the history of film in relationship to the major art movements of the 20th century. Students view and analyze films by such directors as Lang, Eisenstein, Bunuel, Brakhage, and Snow; these films are discussed in the light of their connection to such influential modern art movements as German Expressionism, Russian Constructivism, Surrealism, Abstract Expressionism and Conceptual Art.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 363, HA 363.

title: Documentary Film

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An intensive study of film as document of time, place and action. Influence of social and artistic context is considered. Attention is largely directed to Canadian documentary films, a leader in this genre today. Films studied may include works by Flaherty, Grierson, Lorentz, Riefenstahl, Wiseman, National Film Board.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 364, HA 364.

title: Experimental Film

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Film as art. Investigates a wide variety of experimental forms and covers a range of historical periods and contexts. Emphasis is placed on analyses of key films and on theories of films developed by both artists and critics. Particular attention is paid to the Canadian experimental tradition.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 365, HA 365.

title: History in Cinema

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Cinema as a product of time and place. Emphasis is placed on the relationship between particular film movements and genres and their historical contexts and on theories about the role and function of film in society.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 367, HA 367.

title: Modern and Contemporary Canadian Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A history of the visual arts (painting, sculpture, installation and performance art) from Tom Thomson and the Group of Seven to the present.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 368B, HA 368, HA 368B.

title: History of Photography

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey of the history of photography from its invention in 1839 until the present. Topics to be addressed include the changing role of the photographer as scientist and artist, the relationship between photography and other visual arts, 19th-century travel photography, women photographers, and the various photographic processes which have been developed in the 150 year history of the medium.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 369, HA 369.

title: Popular Film and Cultural Theory

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A study of popular film and its social and political function. Special attention is paid to mainstream films, especially Hollywood genre films, in the interest of exploring the ideological significance of popular film. An exploration of divergent views on the role of popular film within cultural theory provides the context for the analysis of selected films.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370A, HA 370, HA 370A, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Horror Cinema

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An exploration of the subgenres and concerns of the horror film. Focuses on various monsters (such as psycho-killers and zombies), as well as the terror generated by technology, scientific practices and mutating bodies. Theoretical perspectives are considered in the interest of investigating the contradictory functions of fear culture.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370C, HA 370C, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Canadian Film

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An exploration of the history, diverse tendencies and key figures in Canadian Film. Includes developments in fiction, documentary and experimental films.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370D, HA 370D.

title: The Family in Film

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An investigation of the family as represented in film. Uses case studies from different regions around the world to explore how cinematic representations define and depict family systems over time. Content may include: issues of identity; dominant tropes for roles within the family; persistent conflicts and their resolution; and shifting definitions of the family.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370E, AHVS 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Apocalyptic Themes in Cinema

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Examines cinematic depictions of world collapse and catastrophe in relation to apocalyptic and post-apocalyptic visions. Content may include recurrent themes and motifs in films depicting "the end of the world," the fears and desires raised by spectacle and spectatorship, and concluding messages about cinematic visions for the future.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370F, AHVS 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Time in Cinema

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An investigation of the numerous ways in which films record, represent and manipulate time. Case studies examine continuity and/or discontinuity, "real time", simultaneity, "slow cinema", changing philosophical and theoretical notions of time.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 370G, AHVS 392 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Chinese Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Introductory survey from Neolithic times to the present. Topics include ritual bronze vessels of the earliest kingdoms, the Chinese transformation of Buddhism and its arts, imperial patronage of painting, the literati tradition of painting and calligraphy, and propagandistic art of the Cultural Revolution. Emphasizes the cultural contexts for Chinese visual culture.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 372A, HA 372.

title: Japanese Art and Architecture

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introductory survey to Japanese visual culture from Neolithic times to present. Topics include Shinto art and ritual, Buddhist art (including Zen), courtly arts, the tea ceremony, erotic prints of the "Floating World," and contemporary art. Focuses on how Japanese artists adapt foreign cultural traditions.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 373A, HA 373, HA 374.

title: Modernism and Modern Art of the Pacific Northwest

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the arts of Alaska, British Columbia, Washington, and Oregon from the 19th century to 1945. Investigates the relationship between "art" and issues such as colonialism, travel and tourism, the potlatch, the prohibition of the potlatch, ethnography, immigration, moral improvement, the Great Depression and modernity.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 381A, HA 381A.

title: Contemporary Art of the Pacific Northwest

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A thematic examination of the arts of the Pacific Northwest from 1945 to the present. May include primitivism, the Northwest School, the Totemland Studio, modern architecture, public art, feminism, postmodernism, the Vancouver school of photography, commemorations of Japanese internment, environmentalism and indigeneity.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 381B, HA 381B.

title: Contemporary Global Art

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Focuses on how contemporary artists from Africa, Asia, Central and South America and Oceania address the impacts of globalization. Topics may include diaspora, Indigeneity, decolonization, activism and the climate emergency.

title: Indigenous Arts of the Arctic and Subarctic

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to arts of the Indigenous peoples of the North American Arctic and Subarctic. Explores cultural contexts, relationships between artistic expression and environment, spirituality, responses of artists to contact with settlers, and contemporary activism about issues such as climate change.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 382A, HA 382, HA 382A.

title: Indigenous Arts of the Southwest, California and Great Basin

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to arts of the Indigenous peoples of the Southwest, California, and the Great Basin. Explores types and styles of art works, cultural contexts, relationships between artistic expression and environment, spirituality, responses of artists to contact with settlers, and contemporary activities.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 382B, HA 382, HA 382B.

title: Indigenous Arts of the Plains, Plateau, Woodlands and Southeast

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An introduction to arts of the Indigenous peoples of the Plains, Plateau, Woodlands and Southeast. Explores types and styles of art works, cultural contexts, relationships between artistic expression and environment, spirituality, and responses of artists to contact with settlers, and contemporary activities.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 382C, HA 382, HA 382C.

title: Special Topics in North American Indigenous Arts

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: An in-depth investigation of a special aspect of, or area in, indigenous arts. Specific topics may vary from year to year.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 383, HA 383 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Arts and Indigenous Ways of Knowing

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

Investigates relevance to addressing global challenges such as climate change and environmental degradation.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 383A, HA 383 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Indigenous Arts and the Internet

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Explores diverse contexts in which North American indigenous arts appear on the Internet, including artists' sites, virtual exhibitions, commercial galleries, discussions of cultural appropriation in social media and sites related to activism. Encourages active thought about the positive and negative impact of the internet.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 383B, HA 383 (if taken in the same topic).

title: Northwest Coast Indigenous Arts and Colonization

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: Investigation of NWC indigenous artists' creative responses to colonization, 1700 to present. Explores vital roles of art in opposing cultural oppression and empowering cultural survival. Content may include artists' responses to colonizers, development of new art forms due to trade and tourist markets, persecution of potlatches and artistic expression, case studies of artists' resistance to oppression; contemporary artists; and arts in relation to current threats to lands and cultures.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 384, HA 384.

title: A Social History of Impressionism

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of the art and lives of the French Impressionists from the 1860s to the 1880s. Examines Parisian street life, dancers, café concerts, tourism sites and popular fashions through the careers of these artists.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 397, HA 397.

title: A Social History of Post-Impressionism

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

Tracks the movement's development in France, Holland, Belgium, Britain and elsewhere. Topics may include anarchism, esoteric spirituality, symbolist literature, small press publishing and the graphic arts.

title: Art and Revolution I

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 398A, HA 392 (if taken in the same topic), HA 398A.

title: Art and Revolution II

groupFilter1.name: Department of Art History and Visual Studies

description: A survey of art's role in radical social and political change from the 1960s to the present. Examines anarchist, anti-authoritarian, and revolutionary movements in the arts. Topics include radical feminist art, the Situationists, Black Panther graphics, German squatter art in the 1980s, relational aesthetics, and post-anarchism and the arts.
supplementalNotes: • Credit will be granted for only one of AHVS 398B, HA 398B.
